Why Rokeby?
At Rokeby we aim to give your son the very best start in life. We want to give him a sound and strong foundation in his Academic subjects, to enable him to develop in Sports, the Arts and an all-round and exciting curriculum with plenty of additional adventures besides.
Headmaster's Welcome
Read the welcome message from Rokeby’s Headmaster, Jason Peck
Ethos
Discover the way we educate and support all of our boys at the school
Our Aim
The five objectives to ensure that each boy is Smart, Skilful and Kind
3D Virtual Tour
Within the virtual tour you will find messages from our Headmaster and other key members of staff.
Sport at a Prep School in South West London: Building Character Through Activity
Arts Week 2026: A Carnival of Creativity
Radio Jackie: Spotlight on the Rokeby Writing Team

Rokeby Round-Up 22-11-2024

I am delighted that you are reading this. It means you have stumbled across one of the best and happiest prep schools in the UK!
‘…he’s so human and real, constantly developing and growing the school.’
When you are thinking about your son’s future I can guarantee one thing: that you want the very best for him. You want his school days to be friendly and fulfilling, to give him real opportunities to learn and develop in a whole range of different areas, to make sure he is able to make real friends and yet get along with everyone.
Well it’s not a decision to take lightly. It is a tough call for most parents. After all, if your son is so young, what will he be like as he matures? What are his emerging strengths and what will his personality be like in two, five or ten years’ time?
So at Rokeby we aim to give your son the very best start in life. We want to give him a sound and strong foundation in his Academic subjects, to enable him to develop in Sports, the Arts and an all-round and exciting curriculum with plenty of additional adventures besides. We want him to be fulfilled and engaged but also to learn the unwritten lessons: how to treat himself well, and others too, to get along with everyone, to achieve in his own right and as part of a team. How to experience success and feel proud, but also to cope with challenges and setbacks. How to gain entry into an excellent senior school…
Rokeby has much to offer:
We achieve all of this by focusing on each boy and by ensuring that we create a calm, positive learning environment in every aspect. We recognise and celebrate the fact that every boy is different, unique and very, very important.
What does a Rokeby boy look like? That’s easy: your son.
If you visit us, you will sense immediately what we have to offer. When Princess Alexandra came to open our new Lower School building and Performing Arts Hall, this is what she wrote: ‘Such a delightful atmosphere pervaded the whole place’
Come and visit, stay for coffee, and see what you think for yourself.
Rokeby School is an independent day preparatory school for boys aged 4 to 13, based on George Road in Kingston upon Thames. The school has an unrivalled reputation for academic success in the Kingston area, alongside strong pastoral care and a broad, all-round curriculum covering sport, the arts and academic subjects.
Yes. Rokeby is a fee-paying independent school, not a state school. As a private pre-prep and prep school it offers small class sizes, individual attention and a broad curriculum that goes beyond the National Curriculum, preparing boys for entry to their senior schools.
Rokeby School is based on George Road, Kingston upon Thames, Surrey KT2 7PB, within easy reach of Kingston town centre. A dedicated school bus service also runs to and from Raynes Park, Wimbledon, Southfields, Putney, Wandsworth, New Malden and Merton Park, making the school accessible to families across South West London.
Rokeby is organised into three sections: the Pre-Prep (Lower School) for boys in Reception to Year 2, the Prep (Middle School) for Years 3 to 6, and Prep 13+ (Upper School) for Years 7 and 8. Boys typically join at 4+, 7+ or 8+, with occasional places available at other entry points.
Rokeby is built around its motto, Smart, Skilful and Kind, with five clear aims guiding how every boy is educated and supported. The school’s most recent Independent Schools Inspectorate report, from November 2023, confirmed that standards were met across leadership, quality of education, pupil wellbeing, and safeguarding, with particular praise for the school’s facilities and academically rigorous curriculum.
Continuous education from 4+ to 13+

Smart, Skilful, Kind from the Very Start
Our Lower School (Reception to Year 2) is where boys aged 4 – 6 begin their journey to becoming smart, skilful, and kind young learners. Led by Lucia Sanderson, Head of Lower School, we provide a warm, structured, and nurturing environment where every boy is known, supported, and encouraged to thrive.
At Rokeby, we understand that the early years are a vital time for growth. That is why our approach blends play-based learning, emotional development, and the building of strong foundational skills in literacy, numeracy, and communication. Through purposeful play and guided exploration, boys develop curiosity, confidence, and a love of learning.
With small class sizes and a focus on nurturing both a love of learning and character, Rokeby’s Lower School lays the foundation for each boy to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally, so that when he leaves Rokeby at 13, he is a confident, positive, happy and successful young man.
Alongside their dedicated class teacher, boys are taught by specialist staff in French, Music, Drama, PSHE, Games, and PE, enriching their learning experience from the very beginning.
We understand the needs of today’s families. That is why we offer wraparound care from 7:30am to 6:00pm, giving working parents the flexibility they need and providing boys with the consistency and comfort of an environment they know and love.
“Childhood should be delightful, exciting, and time for a child to take in the world with their senses. Each child progresses at their own pace, please try not to worry about what your son can or can’t do at this stage. What matters most is that your son is ready to begin his learning journey. Boys join us from age 4 and have many years of learning, discovering, and development ahead of them. It’s a journey, not a race and we are here to support them all the way through.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Ethos | Smart, Skilful and Kind | Rokeby School
pageCache.text:
Your son comes first.
‘…taking into account every boy’s strengths, interests and individual needs when devising their learning plans.’
We pride ourselves on the ways in which we educate and support all of our boys at Rokeby. We treat them as individuals: we focus on each and every boy. We want each boy to achieve his best in every area of learning so that they become smart, skilful and kind and leave us confident and positive, happy and successful.
There are many ways in which our boys achieve but they always do so when motivated and happy, with the right blend of support and challenge. We give our boys the opportunity to develop skills in a range of activities beyond the core academic subjects, helping them to find things they enjoy and build their confidence, which then benefits their academic studies and personal development. We focus on their strengths but want them to develop competence and confidence in many areas.
We want all of our boys to know that the essence of achievement lies in what they themselves can do and what they can take pride in; that it is not so much about competition with other pupils as with trying to gain the best for themselves from the wealth of opportunities our staff and facilities offer. This demands dedicated teaching, enthusiastic children and good partnership work with parents; and we are committed to this team approach.
A safe and inclusive environment for all
Rokeby School Is committed to providing a safe and inclusive learning environment for all members of our school community. We celebrate diversity and respect the individuality of each boy and staff member. Discrimination, harassment, and bullying based on protected characteristics as defined by the Equality Act 2010 will not be tolerated within our school.

Continuous education from 4+ to 13+

Languages at Rokeby focus on enabling boys to express themselves with confidence and competence.
Our Reception boys are introduced to French via weekly reading lessons. Years 1 and 2 are taught the basics of French in a weekly 20-minute session. They then continue learning the language for the rest of their time at Rokeby. To combine oral fluency with grammatical accuracy, equal emphasis is given to the four skills (reading, writing, speaking and listening).
We take our boys to visit France in Year 6 (Provence or the Loire Valley) and Year 7 (French battlefields, Normandy or Paris) so they can communicate with native French speakers to develop their skills and confidence further.

We focus on teaching our boys to be effective orators and confident readers with a broad-ranging literary interest. Both non-fiction and fiction texts are studied throughout the school year and set texts, studied over the course of a term, are often altered to reflect the current zeitgeist or a theme of particular interest to many boys.
‘Cosy upper school library has brightly coloured chairs, well stocked shelves and a cheery librarian…’
Grammar and spelling are taught from the youngest year groups to ensure a secure understanding of the English language and the ways it can be manipulated for effect. In Year 6, in preparation for pre-tests, the foundations of grammar are cemented, alongside additions of more advanced syntax and punctuation.
Creative writing is taught through multiple stimuli: texts, photo or picture prompts and animations. We encourage pupils to practise writing for a wide range of purposes from creative writing and poetry to formal letters and speeches.
We have an excellent and well-resourced library with an engaging and highly literary librarian always on hand to help. We host some of the best children’s authors and poets to visit us and deliver workshops throughout the year, which adds to the variety and excitement of our English teaching.
Boys are encouraged to take part in a variety of Inter-House Competitions including Debating, Poetry Performance, Scrabble Tournaments and Spelling Bees.

Geography at Rokeby aims to encourage pupils’ curiosity and fascination about the world around them, both now and in the future, on local, national, international and global scales.
Geographical knowledge, understanding and skills provide the frameworks and approaches that explain how the Earth’s features are shaped, interconnected and change over time. The syllabus equips pupils with knowledge about diverse places, people, resources and natural and human environments, together with a deep understanding of the Earth’s key physical and human processes.

We encourage our boys to consider how the past influences the present.
‘and history teacher who actually brings the past to life.’
We take a chronological approach to the teaching of History. The journey begins at Year 1 with the study of prehistory and over the years boys work their way through the ancient civilisations, invaders and settlers, Middle Ages and by the time they reach Years 7 and 8 we reach the start of the 20th Century.
Boys explore source material, weigh it up and reach their own conclusions. They research and sift through evidence so as to be able to argue a point of view, to learn about the past in Britain and the wider world.
We encourage our boys to explore cross-curricular links wherever possible. We organise regular trips to sites of historical interest and incorporate learning history into other residential trips.

We pride ourselves on developing strong Mathematical skills in our boys.
As early as possible, we place an emphasis on developing numeracy, practical Maths, good mechanical skills and logical thinking in problem solving.
We encourage the boys to enjoy Mathematics and to experience it inside and outside the classroom. Boys are placed in sets according to their ability in Year 5. From Year 5 upwards our boys participate in Primary and Junior Maths challenges. Small groups of boys from Year 4 upwards regularly participate in Maths challenges and other competitions.
We provide our boys with a range of enrichment activities including Mathematics sessions during Arts Week and Science Week and trips to St Albans Cathedral and Bletchley Park.

We teach our boys to understand the foundational values of humanity.
Our approach encourages boys to learn about the values of humanity as demonstrated in its diverse cultures.
Study of the major religions forms the basis of the syllabus in Years 3-6. In the top years the emphasis shifts to ethics where we look at the history of civil rights and slavery in Year 7. In Year 8, we then explore and debate ethical issues such as just war, capital punishment, animal testing and free speech. Also, in Year 8, boys undertake an extended project on the Scandinavian prison system.
We teach our boys to respect other cultures and encourage them to discuss how beliefs and values can be applied to contemporary issues in modern society. We develop cross-curricular links and often arrange trips to places of worship.

At Rokeby School, science lessons teach the boys to observe and engage with our planet and everything on it.
We are really lucky at Rokeby to have two fully equipped laboratories and a laboratory technician to help provide memorable learning experiences, with lots of practical classes and experiments to support the scientific theory.
The boys will have great opportunities to observe and investigate the world around them and hone their scientific skills in way that they can conduct experiments, handle the resulting data and make conclusions based on those results.

At Rokeby, our Classics teaching encompasses both the language of Latin and Greek but also many aspects of the civilisations of Rome and Greece and to do this in a stimulating and engaging way.
All boys are given an introduction to the ancient Greek and Roman world in Year 2. They begin learning Latin in Year 5 and continue through to Year 8. Greek is offered as an extra-curricular lesson, to those most able in Latin in Year 7 & 8. The Classics department runs two very successful trips in Year 7 to the Roman baths in Bath and a trip to Italy, biannually, for Years 7 & 8.

We equip boys to use computational thinking and creativity to create programs, systems, and a range of content.
In our weekly ICT lessons, we emphasise building confidence in our boys’ use of a range of computing devices and software packages. Pupils become digitally literate – able to use and express themselves through information and communication technology.
A strong, cross-curricular approach underpins boys’ learning. ICT is integrated into the timetabled curriculum across the school. Each classroom is equipped with an interactive touch screen TV, Apple TV, and computer, and boys in Year 6 and above enjoy the benefits of a 1:1 iPad deployment programme. Utilising iPads allows boys to work with greater emphasis on creativity, collaboration, and higher-order thinking across the curriculum. Laptops are also available to support learning in all age groups.
Our boys are introduced to ICT from their first few days in Reception, through the use of the interactive whiteboard with their class and independent use of laptops within the classroom.

Drama is an integral part of life at Rokeby
‘…gorgeous performing arts theatre…’
We have specialist teachers who help our boys develop craft, interpersonal skills and self-confidence. A number of our boys gain Drama scholarships to top senior schools.
Our curriculum is designed to allow Drama-specific techniques to be developed alongside teamwork, communication and presentation skills; whilst also developing self-confidence, self-esteem and self-reflection.
The development of skills is framed within a narrative structure that is engaging for our boys. In the lower school, narratives are linked to class topics wherever possible to enrich the work covered in class.
Boys have weekly Drama lessons taught by a specialist teacher from Reception to Year 4, and as part of the Arts Carousel through Years 5 – 8. All boys are given the opportunity to work towards Arts Award qualifications as part of the Drama curriculum.
Performing
‘…charismatic drama specialist (‘we do loads of the backstage stuff like lighting too,’ said one boy)…’
There are a wide variety of performance opportunities open to our boys each year including nativity performances in Reception – Year 2, an annual Year 2 and 3 production, participation in the National Shakespeare Schools Festival in Year 7 and the annual senior production for boys in Years 5 – 8.
In addition to the larger productions, all classes present class assemblies throughout the year and for boys who want to get more involved in drama there are weekly drama clubs and LAMDA sessions.
A number of boys have been successful in gaining Drama scholarships to senior schools, including King’s College School, Epsom College, Reed’s School and Tonbridge School.

Rokeby has a flourishing Music department
All boys from Reception to Year 8 benefit from weekly class music lessons. Topics of study include singing, recorder, music theory, ukulele, African drumming, samba, keyboards, Garageband, composition, and in Year 4, violin tuition for a term and a half. Boys also work towards their Bronze Arts Award in Year 7.
Around half of the boys learn musical instruments and our team of 10 eminent visiting teachers offer lessons in singing and the whole range of instruments. Our annual instrumental and singing competitions, the Rowe Cup and Allen Cup take place in the Spring term. In addition to these major events, we have a Carol Concert and Summer Concert and hold smaller, informal year group concerts and workshops.
Our busy weekly programme of ensembles, which includes Year 2, Junior, Senior, and Chamber Choirs, a Wind Ensemble, three String Ensembles, a Cello Ensemble, and a Guitar Ensemble, provides a huge number of boys with the experience and enjoyment of making music in all its forms. Boys can try the viola and cello in Year 1 and 2 in our Lower School ensembles.
Rokeby boys regularly receive Music scholarships to senior schools, including in recent years to St Paul’s, Hampton and King’s College.
